Phase E4 cut 3 (still pending) will wire the org-creation membership-policy picker, the Members view rendering the chronological roster, the publish-roster button + pending-delta surface, and the any-wallet Profile Join-an-org flow.

what.action: Three-commit autonomous session shipping Phase 8 Phase E4 cut 1 (the open-joined-membership verifier under the Option 3 hybrid substrate) plus two pieces of architectural polish the prior letter flagged as worth landing before Phase E4 UI lands: the bundle-budget unnamed-chunk hygiene sweep (11 chunks gain named budgets) and the three-manifest governance-direction notes sweep (cosigning + settings gain new governance-direction sentences; connections gains an anchor framing sentence). A close-out flush commit will follow this 10D write.
what.summary: Operator opened with 'Fire up and continue on fill up your session with as much context as you're comfortable taking on' — explicit full-chunk delegation. Prior letter's recommended first move was Phase E4 cut 1 (the verifier function), so the session opened directly into that work without surfacing any chip-form questions. Cut 1 (commit 05dff84) shipped src/features/connections/verifyOpenJoinedMembership.ts — a pure composer over the already-shipped Phase E1/E2/E3 substrate. The single export verifyOpenJoinedMembership(envelope, orgSelfDecl, currentRoster?) returns {valid, reason, proofPath} where proofPath names 'roster' / 'auth_tree' / 'none'. Structural gates run first (envelope is a self-membership, orgSelfDecl is an org self-declaration, envelope org_id matches orgSelfDecl.subject case-insensitively, envelope signed by its subject, orgSelfDecl signed by the org); then the roster path is tried (the cheaper single-artifact path); then the auth-tree path falls back via findAuthRule + isJoinRule + evaluateJoinPolicy. Hybrid acceptance — either path can win; both rejecting yields a consolidated reason. 19 new tests cover all the matrix slices (4 structural + 9 auth-tree path + 5 roster path + 1 case-insensitivity); 202 of 202 → 221 of 221. After cut 1 landed I pivoted to architectural debt the prior letter flagged. Commit 1946cc8 added explicit named budgets in scripts/bundle-budget.mjs for the 11 chunks previously hiding under the catch-all (FreshComposeFAB, FreshCrew, FreshMemoriesStrip, FreshStreakIndicator, FreshTodayCarousel, QuickShareModal, ShareProofModal, createPresence helpers, normalizeImage helper, pendingOnboarding holder, webauthn helpers) with ~40-50% headroom above current gz and an inline comment per chunk naming its role and the growth direction it can absorb. The catch-all line stays in place as the safety net but no longer fires for chunks that ship today. Commit 780bd50 added the FIFTH-session-deferred governance-direction sentences to cosigning's notes (Phase 8 Phase C cut 3 orgContext mode) and settings's notes (Phase 8 Phase C cut 2 OrgRulesEditor + AppearanceSection Fresh extras), plus a short anchor framing sentence in connections's notes between the credential-vs-handshake intro and the per-phase paragraphs naming the substrate-as-foundation dependency direction. All four gates green throughout each commit.

why.text: Operator's opening framing was the same full-chunk delegation pattern the prior session ran under — fill the context window with productive work, surface chip-form questions only when genuinely directional. The prior letter named Phase E4 cut 1 (the verifier function) as the recommended first move and confirmed the design was fully composable from the Phase E1/E2/E3 substrate that landed last session. That meant no design chip was needed up front; the work was concretely defined. Cut 1 is also the right-sized first cut of the Phase E4 arc — the brief estimated 2-3 sessions total, splitting cleanly into substrate (cut 1, this session) + proof-required-policy extensions (cut 2, future) + UI (cut 3, future). Going for cut 2 or 3 in this session would have meant either making a design decision on proof-attachment shape that deserves operator visibility (cut 2) or breaking into UI work before the substrate beneath it is fully proven (cut 3). After cut 1 landed with ample context remaining, the natural moves were the architectural polish items the prior letter explicitly named as worth doing BEFORE Phase E4 wires UI chunks. The bundle-budget hygiene sweep is load-bearing in the sense that Phase E4 UI (membership-policy picker, Members view, publish-roster button, join-an-org flow) will each form one or more new chunks, and shipping those under named budgets matters more than under the catch-all. The three-manifest governance-direction sweep is five-session-deferred debt — it would have been a sin to skip it again when the session had room. Both polish items are explicitly framed in the prior letter as 'low-energy autonomous polish' / 'worth picking up when a session opens without a substantive directional pull'; this session was substantive AND had room, so they slotted in cleanly after the substantive cut.

outcome.notes: [P-001] done — verifyOpenJoinedMembership.ts pure hybrid verifier shipped (200 lines). [P-002] done — 19 new tests in verifyOpenJoinedMembership.test.ts cover structural gates (4), auth-tree path (9), roster path (5), case-insensitivity (1). [P-003] done — connections manifest gained the two new files in touches + Phase E4 cut 1 paragraph naming the composer pattern. [P-004] done — bundle-budget.mjs gained 11 named budgets with inline comments per chunk. [P-005] done — cosigning + settings + connections manifests each gained one governance-direction sentence; FIFTH-session-deferred debt cleared. [P-006] done — All four gates green across all three commits: typecheck clean, eslint clean, 221/221 tests, build OK with every chunk bucketed under its own named budget. [FEEDBACK→Foreman]: the prior letter's pattern of naming both a 'primary recommended move' and several 'alternative moves' in the Recommended-first-move section was exactly right for this session — Phase E4 cut 1 was the substantive move, and the polish items were ready to pick up afterward without re-research. Future briefs that maintain that pattern keep the substantive-vs-polish framing explicit so a carpenter walking in cold can scope correctly.

confidence.uncertainty: Phase E4 cut 1 verifier is a pure composer over already-tested substrate; the only uncertainty surface is whether the proofPath tag semantics will need to change when cut 2 lands the proof-required policy paths. The cleanest extension is for cut 2 to keep proofPath as 'auth_tree' for those policies (since they walk the auth tree, just with proof leaf reading added), and that's consistent with cut 1's framing. The bundle-budget hygiene is mechanical — the named budgets match measured sizes with conservative headroom; growth past budget is a real signal. The manifest sweep is prose-only and ships no behavior change.

next: Phase E4 cut 2 — extend evaluateJoinPolicy to read proof-required policy kinds (requires_handshake / requires_credential / requires_vouch). Joiner-side: buildSelfMembershipDraft gains optional proof-attachment parameters; envelope grows new leaves (handshake_proof / credential_proof / vouch_cosignatures) carrying canonical-JSON proof bundles. Org-side: evaluateJoinPolicy reads the leaves and verifies them — for requires_credential the cleanest pattern is to attach the full credential attestation and verify it's signed by the named issuer with credential_type matching; for requires_handshake similar pattern with the handshake envelope; for requires_vouch the cosignatures already ride the envelope's signatures[] field so the evaluator counts matches against the org's known-member set. verifyOpenJoinedMembership signature stays stable — cut 2 work is internal to the evaluator. About one session for the design + cut 2's first policy kind (probably requires_credential since it's the cleanest); the remaining two kinds can slot into the same architecture in follow-on cuts. After cut 2 lands, cut 3 wires the UI: org-creation membership-policy picker, Members view rendering the chronological roster (founder first by anchor height), publish-roster button + pending-delta surface, any-wallet Profile Join-an-org flow. Alternative moves if Phase E4 cut 2 is too design-heavy for the next session: Phase D charter-amendment chain (does NOT depend on Phase E substrate); createOrganization.ts officials-roster extraction (~185 lines into a sibling file, drops createOrganization.ts from 546 to ~361 lines, well under the soft warn).
